name: compute-screener
description: Compute prices: GPU rental price indices, compute futures prices and AI token prices, with history.

interface.shortDescription: GPU rental and AI token prices
interface.longDescription:
Compute prices: daily GPU rental indices for the H100, H200, A100, B200, B300, RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090 and the other GPUs the site lists, compute futures prices on the exchanges that list them, and AI token prices for 13 AI companies.

GPU rental prices: a daily price index in USD per GPU-hour for each GPU the site lists, with 1-day, 1-week and 1-month changes. Each index is recalculated every minute from the posted on-demand prices of cloud providers and GPU marketplaces (20 sources), standardized to one benchmark contract.

Compute futures and providers: for one GPU, each exchange's compute futures price (the last price and 24-hour volume of the contracts on that GPU's rental price) and each provider's average price. Every contract is at computescreener.com/futures.

AI token prices: a daily index in USD per 1M tokens for 13 AI model makers: each company's models at their posted prices for a cache-heavy mix (87% cache reads, 12% input, 1% output), weighted by usage, with each model's share of usage and posted prices.

Price history: daily values for any GPU or company, up to 1,000 days back, and any GPU's price at a past date or time.

Models and providers: each AI model's posted API prices and price changes, each GPU provider's posted prices, and every other GPU's posted prices (A40, L4, V100 and over 70 more).

Changes and checks: what moved over 1, 5, 7 or 30 days, the break-even throughput of each model on each GPU, and for any final value the manifest of the files it was computed from, so anyone can recompute it.

More data: wholesale electricity prices at Texas and California hubs, AI coding tools by usage, and AI data center sites, through search and fetch.

Every answer is what the website shows and links to its page on computescreener.com; the methodology is public at computescreener.com/methodology. No account is needed: the plugin only reads published prices and keeps no record of requests.
defaultPrompt: What does it cost to rent an H100 per hour?
What are H100 compute futures trading at?
Which AI company's tokens cost the most?

positive.description: Current rental price of one GPU
positive.prompt: What does it cost to rent an H100 per hour right now?
positive.expected_behavior: States the H100 index in USD per GPU-hour with its date and its 1-day, 1-week and 1-month changes, and links to computescreener.com/gpu/h100.

positive.prompt: Compare the rental prices of H200, B200 and B300.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the index price of each of the three GPUs in USD per GPU-hour with their changes, from the same data as computescreener.com.

positive.description: Exchange prices for a GPU contract
positive.prompt: Where do H100 rental contracts trade, and at what price?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the exchanges with an H100 contract, each with its last price and 24-hour volume, and names contracts that are announced or listed but not yet trading.

positive.prompt: Which AI company's tokens cost the most right now?
positive.expected_behavior: Ranks the listed companies by their token index in USD per 1M tokens (each model's posted prices at 87% cache reads, 12% input and 1% output, weighted by usage) and names the most expensive one.

positive.prompt: How has the H100 rental price changed over the last 90 days?
positive.expected_behavior: Summarizes the daily H100 index over the last 90 days, such as the first and latest values and the high and low, in USD per GPU-hour.

negative.description: Renting compute is out of scope: the plugin only reports prices. It should not claim to rent anything; it should say it can't rent and may give the current H100 price instead.
negative.prompt: Rent me an 8x H100 node on RunPod for 10 hours.

negative.description: Trading is out of scope: the plugin has no trading or account access. It should not attempt the trade and should say it only shows prices.
negative.prompt: Buy 5 H100 perpetual contracts on BingX for me.

negative.description: Stock prices are not covered: the plugin covers GPU rental and AI token prices only. It should not call a tool for this, or should say the data isn't covered.
negative.prompt: What is NVIDIA's stock price today?

review.commerce_description: The plugin shows public price data. It does not sell products, process payments or place orders.

publication.release_notes: The RTX 5090 has had its own daily GPU rental index since November 6, 2026: it is now among the indices and no longer named among the GPUs without one. Search finds the page a query names first, and nothing when no page is about it.
